t:
I know captain's got a stash!

I noticed him when he approached it. He pushed something, and the stash opened.

I've got to check it out when nobody sees me.

If there's gold, I'll just sneak out quietly and go on the run.

Captain's been holding grudge after that girl wandered away under my supervision, he could throw me overboard.

Damnit! Why did I allow Boko to talk me into this in the first place?
Now I'll be cursed forever!

I am nobody... Hah! I am nobody!
I am just a shadow in the night!
I am forever dead... Thank Tep!
You can see outlines of a ghostly figure on the stone... This spirit, trapped by Tep's magis, seems to be trying to tell you something.

I am not going to give up!
Argh! If only I could get out of here! I'd teach that Beak a lesson not to betray friends!

Nonsense! That's just an old wives' story! This is all because of Boko the Fierce. He was an Orcish Prospector that earned his living by trading artifacts, but then he vanished into thin air! We all thought he was dead, but then I heard that he was spotted in Nezebgrad. He bought an Astral ship and a ton of other things at the auction house. He really threw his money about.
I assume he made a fortune off a rare artifact somehow.
Hello. Do you want to talk about something?

With the frequency I get asked about this question, I should write the story down on a piece of paper and hang it above the entrance to the Inn... Well, listen up because I'm not going to repeat this.
There was a Prospector named Boko the Fierce who lived here not long ago. He found out about this legend and wanted to find this "Wish Maker" and make his dearest wish come true. He found another three idiots and together they went searching. No one has heard from his companions ever since.
I bet he killed his three companions and stole their belongings. That's how he could afford to go back to Nezebgrad and buy a ton of things. I'm sure it was dirty money. What a bastard.
Do you have a question for me? Don't hesitate to ask! I'll gladly give you an answer!

Hm...
I've heard this legend before. Tep's ancient and powerful artifact that can grant any wish. Maybe it's true, maybe it isn't.
One thing I know for sure is that nothing good can come from Tep! He was the reason my people perished!
Care for a piece of advice? Stay out of it. You will regret it later, but it will be too late.
Would you like to buy something, or are you here about something else?

Argh! You're all the same! How many times do I have to say that I know nothing about it? Yes, Boko belonged to my clan! Yes, he became fabulously rich and bought a whole allod, but I have no idea where he got the money! I don't want to hear anything about him!
That Boko disgraced my clan! He was nothing but a mean bastard! I'm sure that whatever he did to get that money, it wasn't legal. I would advise you not to follow in his footsteps.
What do you want? Speak quickly, I'm busy!
Before I give it to you, vow that you will pay a better attention when dealing with such things!
Take this banner! It will help you with your mission.

To use the items pu-... put them on the... the hillside... The first one needs to...
Oh, who's there?
I will help you bind your Adventurer's Stone to this location.
This allod is decaying... those demons will pay!
What's that? A contract agreeing to provide supplies for an Astral ship? Hmm... well, you have done great services to the Free Traders on the battlefield. We would be happy to accept your business!
Well done! Well, you've managed to complete the task, but this isn't the end you know!
This golem doesn't seem to show any signs of life. What a curious creature. Perhaps it only moves when it's alone with its fellow golems.
Hm, you have helped the Historians out immensely. Take this contract - we'll help you build your ship. May your journeys be heroic enough to warrant recording in our history books!
We cannot win this war against the demons alone. The whole world must band together. I hope you understand that.
Hm. Well, the more heroes there are roaming the Astral, the worse it will be for the demons. Here, I will gladly give you a contract and promise to help with your Astral ship.
You lost it already? You need to learn to take better care of your gear. It could mean the difference between victory and defeat in this war. Here, take another whistle and don't lose it!
Where would you like to go?
I am the Crossing Keeper. Where would you like to go?
I will help you bind your Adventurer's Stone to this location.
Greetings, traveler. I will send you back to Polis.

Are you eager for glory? Do you love fighting? Then you're in the right place! Right behind me is the Arena of Death. It's a place where many of your kind gather to fight to the death! I can send you there if you wish.

What, the command finally came to its senses? Now they remember me and those poor soldiers guarding The Sweety!
What are you doing here?

It's a hard time for us. These beasts are everywhere! It looks like my Sweety attracts them like some sort of astral honey.
We need your help.
You don't have enough money to do that.
What are you doing here? Still want to capture our Kirah? Invader!

It's a hard time for us. These beasts are everywhere! It looks like my Sweety attracts them like some sort of astral honey.
We need your help.
Hello there! How can I help you?
These ancient June ruins are overflowing with magic...

Greetings, Seeker of Truth!
The portal I'm guarding will send you to your ship in the Astral Hangar.

Greetings, Seeker of Truth!
The portal I'm guarding will send you to the Citadel.
You can use it to travel between Citadel and your faction's capital. You can bind your Adventurer's Stone to this portal.
We are happy to see you here in the Citadel!

Greetings, Seeker of Truth!
Here, on the Terrace of Truth, you will find Master's attendants who are awaiting visitors to convey them the Master's will. They will happily share their wisdom, knowledge and powers accumulated through thousand years of their service!

I am Guardian of Anger.
Anger is blinding and mind-blurring. It forces you to make hasty decisions. The one who surrenders to Anger makes mistakes where cool-headed doesn't move a muscle. Control your Anger!
You managed to overcome the five sins. The road to Revelation is open. This Shard of Crystal Armor is your first step to understanding the Truth!
Hello there! How can I help you?
Are you sure you want to bind to this location?

I can't send you directly to the Citadel until the Twilight Isle portal is not connected with the Isle of Revelation portal. But I can teleport you to a smaller isle with ancient ruins from which you can get to the Citadel by yourself.
Here, and good luck in your heroic deeds!
Here, and good luck in your heroic deeds!

You! How can you doubt my words? I've warned you that the poison Sarn's minions pour into your ears, can be lethal.
Oh, Sarn... His flattering speeches compelled me to fight him and put him into the most secure prison in the Universe, but even this could not make him mend his ways. My bitter friend understood nothing. He can't live without a crowd of spongers around him...
Is it their lies that made you doubt, if only for a second, that those madmen are our enemies? Wake up! Their goal is to destroy the world! Your world, by the way, where you will still have to live.
I gave you a chance to examine the cult of Sarn from the inside to help expel whatever doubts you may have harbored about who the true enemy of this world is. Look, it doesn't particularly affect me either way: I am a god and I can easily reduce Sarn to jelly along with all his minions. But that would be boring! The problems of this world shall be solved by its inhabitants. And if you care about your own future and the future of Sarnaut, you know what you need to do to ensure its safety.

You are surprised why the portal to the Dead City is not working, are you? You are right to be surprised. But I have an idea what might be the issue. Oh, no, it's not because of "astral storms" or other whirls.
You see, my friend, it seems to me that cultists simply cheated you. They used you and other adventurers like you to exact revenge on their enemies - wormfaces and draconids. Not only that, they managed to get hold of the fragments of one of my seals... Which puts you in quite a pickle...
You don't really expect them to readily share with you the keys to the Dead City, do you? Ha-ha-ha! The bait I tossed them is too yummy to share.

D'you want to know what it's like to be a demiurge? The Creator of the worlds and the universe itself? To raise land out of ocean depths and bring down mountains with a wave of your hand? To extinguish stars with a single word? Fat chance! It can't be that something is created out of nothing. Everything in the universe obeys basic laws, even gods. Yes, we can create worlds, but this process is complex, time-consuming and not very entertaining. Thankfully, the two of us don't need a whole world.
You (with my help, of course) will become a creator of a new allod! You will use your will and power to open a path to this allod. You will create a new portal that will be independent from the cultists or wormfaces and lead directly to your destination - the Dead City!
Wormfaces, draconids, demons and Chosen Ones... The game's gaining momentum!
Are you sure you want to bind to this location?
These ruins can transport you in a number of locations.
The stone I'm about to give you will teleport you to the grates. These are invisible passageways underneath Gipat. You can use them to travel faster around the world.
Here it is. Please, don't lose it again. This stone is a sign of great trust. Only those who have completed the Path of Revelations are granted one. You'd be wise to guard it well.
The terrible demons are now dead and my soul is no longer tormented. Thank you for avenging my death.

I didn't need your help. I could have done it myself, you know.
Hm, an enemy of the Empire helping me. It looks like some things really have changed in this world. How strange...
These ancient June ruins are overflowing with magic...
These ancient June ruins are overflowing with magic...
You can bind to this location for returning here later.
These ancient June ruins are overflowing with magic...
These ancient June ruins are overflowing with magic...

Ah, the Imperial... enemy...
What do you need?
Now that I've been avenged I am no longer tormented. Thank you for your help.
I guess I don't need anything anymore. It's good to know that we can fight together, like our fathers in the Great Astral Campaign...
My magic will change the outcome of this battle! You must protect me!
I will not forget your help.
Please say you have some magical charges! We need more!
Thank you. Now we can overcome the demons!
Those damn demons! There are too many of them and not enough magical charges!
Thank you. Without your aid, all would be lost.
Did you bring any magical charges?
Thank you! You're a real hero!
Please say you have some magical charges! We need more!
Just in time. Now we have a chance to win this battle!
Pain, away with you! Do not disturb me!
Without more magical charges it'll be very difficult for me to maintain this.
Thank you! These will be very helpful.
Use the ruins to teleport to one of the destination points.

You can still call me Gorislav, as you used to. Or if you wish, call me Director.
As for my true name... The answer will come in time. The Time will call my name!

You see, a certain event occurred about a century ago that put at risk all our current attempts to withstand both demons and the Power that controls them. If we change the Past, our present lives will be so much easier!
Besides, we'd better deliver a strike when our enemy least expects it. Sarn is not prepared now. I think this is a great opportunity!

In the middle of the Crossroads there is a Whirlpool of Time - a vortex where the Past that came to be, the unstable Present, and the variable Future are swirling.
The Whirlpool of Time is dangerous. An unexperienced time traveler would rather drown themselves than appear in the right place at the right time. But don't worry - I will teach you everything you need to know.
Still, we require something else but your bravery and my powers. Time is always hungry for blood, but we can deceive it.

The Ashes of the Past! The Time would prefer to devour this magic substance over you. Every time you travel to the Past, you have to feed Time with this delicacy.
You can find the Ashes of the Past on an Isle called the Astral Graveyard.

The main change you triggered is that the great battle between the League and the Empire has ceased to be! The Expeditionary Corps and The Regiment of Kirah never engaged into the bloodshed, they came prepared for the demon assault.
Of course, demons pummeled both armies, but not as severely as they used to.
As a result, demons had to change their tactics. But more on that later...
Your actions had other consequences as well. Yasker, for one, became terrified of zombies and decided to study necromancy deeper. So we are not sure of the outcome of his battle against Eniel.
On the other hand, having witnessed the resurrection, Negus Tot did not put much trust in science and confided in religion instead. Nobody knows yet what it means for us.
The mysterious demon you encountered was an assassin whose only goal was killing you. Our enemy knows that we want to change the Past, and he made his move.

As you may guess, we shall not lay our arms down. There is something we should change in the Past. It is no less important than the prevention of war or the salvation of Kirah. We will do it, and no assassins will stop us!

If you have read the chronicles of the past, you might remember what they say about demon intrusion to Kirah. Let me cite it for you...
"First fell the tower of Vlad, the Great Xadaganian Mage..."
Can you see any towers here?
There is none. Vlad is here, but no tower around. Why? Because Vlad has never been a Great Mage!

Vlad is a guardian of the most important Nezeb's treasure hidden on Kirah. Of course he isn't a Great Mage! Nezeb would have never trusted his treasure to one!
To be honest, the League is here not for Meteoric Iron either. Tensess was looking for the treasure, too. Now you know the secret that only Yasker and Eniel were aware of.

All right, I shouldn't keep you in the dark any longer. The treasure is a heart of a Great Dragon killed thousands years ago by June people. You know, Great Dragons are immortal by nature. It seems Junes went to a great length to kill one. And even now, long after his death, the Heart of a Great Dragon is bleeding.
This blood holds the secrects of the immortality of the Great Mages.

All candidates in the Conclave had to drink this blood as the last step of their trial. Dragon's blood flows in the veins of each Great Mage. They have to renew it regularly, but finding a Great Dragon is no small feat nowadays. And of course, dragons hate Great Mages. Soliskar the Wise had to make sure there are no Great Mages among Demon Hunters before forging an alliance with them. She will never befriend Historians, for example. Did you happen to bring a strange potion to Zayan de Desirae, back when he fought vampires? Well it was the vial of the Dragon's Blood.

Now you must understand everything. Eniel is on mission from Tensess to retrieve the Dragon's Heart, while Yasker is trying to keep it, fulfilling Nezeb's will. And I want you to outsmart them both.
No, I'm not a Great Mage, and I need the Dragon's Heart for reasons other than immortality... I'm not much interested in one, you know.
This is what I wanted to tell you. Much of your knowledge about this world is based on lies. Trust me, and you will learn the truth.

Of course, this is not the best body, but I am thankful to be alive.
I am looking forward to eating, boozing, and chasing some Chosen skirts. In time, I may even get used to looking at myself in the mirror.

Ha, what do I care about that name? Their leader could be a mulberry bush for all I care!
Let them worship a cup of tea or dragon dung, what's it to me? You'll have to excuse me for not wanting to be disembodied again. I can't even stand to think about it. I bet my boots we can find out that name some other way.

Well, so what? So what if I spend half the day squatting behind the bushes! We are used to it.
As long as nice big leaves are at hand, we're content. As for my liver... I am going to jump from the allod every Mardi Gras. Death cures all diseases and maladies. Why do you think we are all so healthy? You probably don't even remember the last time you sneezed.
The more you die, the healthier you are.

That is so simple! Good thinking, too! We cannot do anything with him, but, fighting as sparks, I can extract every name from him. Up to seventh generation!
Hey, why are you looking away? Are you plotting something? Oh, you want to lure me out, so he could quietly enter my body? Like hell, noble gents! Osip is not a simpleton!

What? All the cultists are castrated? All right, turn around, let me check...
Oh, hell in a basket! There is nothing to castrate here!
To hell with this life? If I were half as depressed as him, I'd join a cult, too. No wench would ever love me as I am.
I did not sign up for that! Hell no, let's trade back. I'd rather be a dead hero's ghost, than a live laughing stock...

The ancient temple of a vanished nation... Whom did they pray to inside it? The only Creator? The local spirits? Great heroes and rulers? What did they sacrifice - incense or some beings' hearts? No one knows that today.

The Defiled Ruins in Gipat were the stage of the final act in the Play where Sarnaut's heroes received the Revelation. I was there too... That's the place I'd never want to come back to!

However, a traveler told me he'd seen a reflection of the Defiled Ruins in the depths of the mysterious Astral: the ruins with evil spirits and demon worshipers wandering around. However, the cultists dug out some June magic machinery in those ruins, and now they're fighting it as they don't know how to put it back in the ground. He also mentioned that the ruins made an unpleasant surprise for him in the end. You ask me, what can be more unpleasant than what we actually found in there? But if you happen to find that reflection, stay sharp!

You know what happened in the Darkblood Citadel. The home of the De Doucer family - a favorite among elite circles for balls and evening parties - has turned into a vampire nest. Armando de Doucer banded together with Tep and led a vampire invasion to Kania and Avilon. Their plans could only be ruined through the intervention of heroes like you... What if it went differently?
Do you know who vampires' worst enemies are? Shapeshifters! That might be linked to the blood curse cast on them both. If you spot the spires of the Darkblood Citadel in the mysterious Astral, get ready to see what would have happened if the shapeshifters had gotten to the vampires before the League heroes had. Keep your eyes open, though: werewolves hate the likes of you only a little less than they do bloodsuckers. Don't get caught between a rock and a hard place!

I believe you are well aware of the notoriety of this place. The patrimony of the noblest aristocrats has turned into a den of evil and the undead. Or, more precisely, that was the case until a squad of the League's daredevils got into the very depths of that hole and put an end to the curse. But what if it went differently?

The mysterious Astral is an enigmatic place. Sometimes it allows you to see what would have happened to the places you know if the events had unfolded differently. The Imperials have nothing to do in the Courtyard - they have more than enough trouble of their own. But what if Kania had been under the rule of the Empire? What if Elizaveta Rysina had sent an elite exorcist corps to the castle and the evil embedded there had gotten hold of their souls?

If you get into the reflection of the Courtyard, beware: those whom you meet there are not real priests, not Imperials and not even people. But the wounds they can inflict on you are quite real... but so are the treasures you will find in the storerooms!

I don't think I need to tell you about Tensess Temple! After all, it was you who had to get through swarms of enemies to reveal the mystery of the gift of Light. I wish I knew what heroes like you saw there and what Tensess' Spark told you. However, a state secret remains a state secret. Instead, I'll tell you what I know about its astral reflection.

The dilapidated sanctuary in the depths of the jungle is the tomb of an ancient mage who rivaled Nezeb himself. You won't find Tensess' Spark in the reflection, but you will find lots of enemies... In this sense, the reflection is very close to reality.

You'll have to defeat five extremely dangerous enemies and a horde of demons at the top of the temple. However, the reward will be worth it! And who knows, maybe the reflection will share new secrets with you!

Oreshek Fortress is the largest and most secure prison of the League. No wonder you never heard of it before - only the most dangerous criminals are put into it, and there's no escape...
The White Knight, Miroslav Kramolsky, was imprisoned here. His Imperial friends arrived and started shooting. They intended to free him and spark the rebellion. The guards stood firm, and the Imperials had to leave empty handed. That was for real. But somewhere in the depths of the Astral, a reflection of the island appeared. There, in this island, Kramolsky broke free, he trapped everyone's soul in the prison, and turned the fortress into his own stronghold. If this scenario were true, both League and Empire would have moaned with despair. This is no joke, one of the strongest keeps in the world, captured by gangsters!

The name of Tep doesn't give the shivers to common people any longer. He was destroyed at Irdrich shards by heroes of the Empire. Of course, the League helped a bit, too. But what if Tep hasn't resurrected? What would have happened to his lair? They say, somewhere in the depths of Astral there is a reflection of Irdrich with no pyramid or cultists, only filled with dark creations of the ancient necromancer that keep on destroying ships and killing Sparks, even without their master. If you ever come across this reflection, be careful. Reflected devices are as dangerous as real ones!
Can't tell you much about these isles, they are too mysterious.

If you ever come across this reflection, be careful. Reflected devices are as dangerous as real ones!
Can't tell you much about these isles, they are too mysterious.

Welcome!

Do you want to learn more about Astral allods and dangerous adventures?

Listen to me then. Who knows, maybe this information will save your life.

I assume you already know that Imperial research in the fields of magic and science is performed in top secret labs.

However, the glorious history of our progress has one dark spot. I am talking about the Lab 9.

Yasskul Skritam, Tep cultist who follows his Master will zealously, has interfered into our experiments and revived the Plague, ancient disease that exterminated the Zem people.

Now the island is in total control of the diseased. There is no possibility to cure them. We can only bring peace to both these people and General Novikov, the head of the Lab 9 now known as Plague General. You also should get rid of infected zombies carrying the disease. And of course you should kill Yasskul Skitram who caused all troubles at the plagued island.

Can you handle it?

Have you ever been to the Vortex Isle?

An icy rock hovering in the Astral. A tomb of the Great Dragon defeated back in June times can be found there. Dragon's ghost has been guarding the Tomb for thousands of years.

There is an abundant supply of meteorite ore on the isle, so we are extremely interested in getting control over it. Perhaps you can help?

Listen carefully. In order to get to the Wraith, you will have to fight Glacier Elementals, Wild Yetis in the cave and Harpies that guard the pass to the Great Dragon's Tomb. Only near the Tomb you will be able to see the Wraith and defeat it.

During my travels I try to keep away from Wolf Island. There is an old legend about this death trap, a Kanian village that became a feeding ground for a werewolf.

A long, long time ago Kanian druid Vseslav the Charming got so close with the wolves from the island that he learned how to transform into one. He became their leader, and his neighbors were his first victims. After a while the whole island became infested with wolves and werewolves. Unlucky travelers who ventured to the island were eaten by predators.

If you want to perform a feat, Wolf island is just the place for it. Here's my advice: think twice before you challenge the pack!

In one of the expeditions I discovered an Astral isle that must have fallen apart from Holy Land. There is a Site of Power on this isle, a rich source of the Holy magic for which both League and Empire would die for.

The trouble is that the local folks have created a cult of blood around it. They are sure that the Gift of Resurrection had been brought to them by the Scorpion King, a giant creature that they call Serket. Both Waterfolks and Forestfolks strive for his grace fighting each other. They sacrifice living creatures to be devoured alive, and these poor victims can never be resurrected. But the people of this isle believe that these sacrifices ensure resurrection to the others.

This amok has to be stopped. It dishonors the idea of the Light. The Empire needs to take this Site of Power under its control! However, the waterfolks and the forestfolks are not going to have you challenge their poisonous king. You will have to fight them first. The waterfolks are the strongest, so they are going to be your primary target.

But your ultimate foe is Serket, the Scorpion King.

Have you heard the legend of the Isle of the Damned? This sad story proves that one evil soul can be worse than the whole world of evil.

Once upon a time there was a small village on some distant Astral island. Nice and honest people lived there. A loving couple was among them - Ivan and Maria, who got married and lived happily.....for a while. It should have been the perfect end of their fairy tale... but it wasn't.

A foreigner lived in that village. He was not a good one, but a man with a greedy and envious soul. He craved Maria's beauty and tried to approach her, but Maria brushed him off.

When Ivan and Maria got married he was out if his mind and decided to ruin their lives. He stole Maria's wedding ring, Ivan's love letter and a bunch of wedding flowers. He used these items to cast an evil curse on the young couple.

They went off to their graves soon and were buried together. But evil does not just vanish - an awful curse fell on the whole island and the villain himself. He died and turned into an undead.

The souls of the young couple remained restless.

They will only find peace when the curse is lifted.

You must find the wedding ring, the letter and the flowers, bring them to the grave and free the poor souls.

I'd never recommend you to mess with Draconids. They are dangerous. Even Demon Hunters who forged an alliance with them don't trust them completely. Why? Because Draconids don't share their secrets to anyone! Even to their friends.

I don't know what they are hiding in their Green Maze. Historians who explored it couldn't get to its depths, the way was blocked with a magic barrier. Once they tried to get through it, two High Draconids, Border Guards as they called themselves, appeared to drive the Historians away. From that day, Draconids would always meet unwelcomed guests with steel.

If you are willing to take a risk, try to solve the mystery of the Green Maze. However, you must find the path into the ancient ruins yourself.

The Silent Hills... I used to visit them quite often. I talked to ordinary Kanian people without fear, enjoyed their delicious fresh bread. Oh what a blessed land... it was.

Now this Isle is haunted. The ghosts live lives like normal people - they fish, hunt, grind flour. But when I arrived there the last time, they were not happy to see me or my crew. We barely escaped!

I'm puzzled! What kind of evil came to Silent Hills? Who cursed these people?

If you're brave enough to challenge this mystery, follow my advice. Search the Dark Forest! This had always been a nasty place. Maybe the evil that had been sleeping there woke up! Your way there will certainly be full of danger.

Remember that you will have to fight the ghosts to cleanse the Isle. This is the pain you will have to overcome. Keep in mind that you're giving them freedom, not death.

My friend Roman Kuzin, traveler and researcher, was unlucky to get stranded on the Lost Isle. I haven't heard from him since then...

The Lost Isle has its legend. This is the legend of Tep's Pyramid that came into its own mind and started raising the undead. People say that the one who manages to conquer the Pyramid, will receive a great treasure.

Roman was dreaming of this adventure. He learned a lot about this island. I will tell you everything I know if you agree to save my friend.

On the Lost Isle you will face Magic Elementals that are spawned by the powers of the Pyramid. You will also come across a lot of undead. Destroy them to get to the Pyramid and find a way to disable it, and you will be rewarded.

So? Will you help me?

What do you know about Goblins?

On the one hand, they are just miserable creatures. Everybody makes fun of them and despises them. There are all sorts of goblin jokes, and they are also known as pets for orc shamans. Sometimes I feel pity for them.

And on the other hand, they are thieves and bandits. Scoundrels, they are always up to something evil! Have you ever met goblin weapon dealers in Coba Plateau? Then you know what I am talking about!

Goblins have their own island in the Astral. This is their citadel, their republic! They even elect a... there's one funny word for it... a President! For the third time in a row they re-elect a shaman named Urub. It's he who's responsible for goblin raids on our allods.

If you happen to find this island, enforce the death sentence to the goblin "President"!

Have you ever heard of the Volcano Isle?

A Draconid tribe used to live on that island. They worshipped the God of Fire, who was sleeping in the crater of the dormant volcano. Sacrifices maintained his sleep and contained his rage.

But when the High Priest of the Draconids died, the knowledge of the ritual was buried with him. The volcano erupted and a powerful fire elemental escaped! He created four guards out of magma and flame - these huge manticores would turn anyone to ashes with their hot breath!

Many Draconids died, but the most cunning of them survived. They bring Crawler hearts in special bowls as sacrifices to protect themselves from fire.

If you ever try to drive the elementals back into the volcano, remember: do not attempt to attack the elemental while the manticores are alive! The God of Fire distributed his power among them, so killing the guards will make him weaker.

That's all I know. Good luck!

During one of my expeditions I was unlucky enough to visit the Tomb Isle. At first it appeared a silent and deserted place, a quiet home to one of Tep's Pyramids.

My second visit was proof of the terrible news of Tep's revived cult. Now his followers rule there. They use rock elementals to dig out the Pyramid. I don't know what they're looking for. They attacked me and my team, my people were badly wounded, so we had to leave the Isle really fast. I feel bad about it.

I'd like to ask you to find this Isle and put an end to the cultists.

I have never been to the Border Isle.

It is called like that because it often floats near Holy Land. It's not a surprise that both League and Empire fought for this allod to use it as a basecamp and to fortify their positions. Alas, the Empire was lucky enough to capture it first.

Anyway, access to the Isle is denied now. The Xadaganian garrison defending the Border Isle has betrayed the Empire! Obviously, demons cultists appeared among the soldiers. Or it may as well have happened because of the Astral worm entrenched in the middle of the Isle... They say it's able to corrupt people's minds.

Izbor Yavorsky himself has recently asked me about heroes willing to help the League. At the moment our army cannot afford sending an expedition to the Isle, but someone has to punish the traitors!

The Isle has to be cleared of the demons!

Maybe you have already encountered creatures corrupted by the Astral. It transforms them, usually for the worse...

Astral Horn is one of these creatures. It's a unicorn that was turned into a dangerous monster. It's not easy to find and very difficult to defeat. But I know a thing that might be helpful...

When you find the Astral Horn Isle, you will have to smash your way through the Astral crystals using the Hammer of Pain. You will get it by defeating Splasher, a fierce water elemental. You will also have to fight against Granite Trolls to find Shards of Pain. Power concealed in them can be used to charge your weapon with magic in the June Ruins guarded by a cyclops called Stomper.

With the charged Hammer, you will be able to break through the magic defenses blocking the way to Horn's den.

I'm not sure what you will find there. Be prepared to anything. I know that Astral Horn is hard to find. It's a master of camouflage.

Good luck!

Oh, you heard the rumors about this island?

A mysterious place. It's an ancient June Forge captured by Tep's cultists. Nobody knows what is happening there. I heard of a group of reckless travelers who dared to enter the depths of the ancient volcano where the Forge is located.

Only one of them came back. He said that cultists are trying to take control over ancient June machines, trying to turn them into their loyal servants. If they succeed...

The June's genius combined with Tep's insanity... Ouch... Be extremely careful if you are up to this adventure.

Who would have thought that people and vampires could live in peace? You wouldn't believe me, but there is such a place! It's called Enoch Island.

It was once a real backwater, with just two towns. Not so long ago some vampires forsook their creator, Armando de Doucer, and arrived on the island. They somehow came to an agreement with the peasants, bartering their own goods, healing magic and other useful things for blood. Everything has changed when the werewolves got to Enoch.

A vicious pack of half-wit beasts came barging in, bringing an end to the peace that the island had once enjoyed. Their chief, Luth the Meager, a former ringleader of a gang of thieves, vowed to devour anyone who failed to bow before him. The vampires protected themselves from the werewolves with a magic barrier, and closed the roads between the villages. Alongside the peasants, they have been resisting the monsters' attacks, but their strength is fading.

So if your travels happen to take you to Enoch Island, be prepared for quite a fight! Before getting at their leader, you will have to cleanse both villages of werewolves.

Yes, I've heard of that town. White 17 is a top secret military settlement, hidden deep in the Astral. You see, Imperial scientists in White 17 were engaged in extremely dangerous research. People say that lead researcher Nomarkh Ebol maintained a close relationship with Yasskul Setnakhte. Well, I've already told you about Setnakhte and the incident at Lab Nine.

We have lost touch with White 17 a short time ago. I'm afraid they got into trouble.

So if you happen to come across the snow-covered isle guarded by Imperial soldiers, I'd suggest you sail away. But should you decide to land, find Valentine Shtammin, a friend of mine and chief engineer there. He is smart, reliable and always ready to help. I have a feeling there is something wrong with White 17...

Once a circus with merry clowns and acrobats, this place did not enjoy much popularity recently. Who would fly through the dangers of the Astral to see a performance? No wonder the isle has come to rack and ruin.

All of a sudden, three guys appeared, who called themselves "masters of dreams". They repaired the old circus building and sent out invitations to a carnival. They promise that their incredible show will fulfill people's long-time dreams and desires.

As for me, I think they are charlatans. They don't want money at all, this is very strange. Be on your guard, it can be a trap!

Abandoned excavation? Oh yes, I remember.

Weird things happened there...

That small island is pierced with caves, like a piece of cheese. The caves were inhabited by kobolds, and old mine tunnels were dwelt by mountainfolks. They lived there until the Empire grabbed hold of the island.

Imperial soldiers kicked the natives out of the caves, brought in a batallion of goblins and started to dig in the mine for gold and gems. They excavated tons of treasures! But then a real bummer happened.

One of the goblins, the most quirky and strong-headed, sealed a deal with kobolds and mountainfolks offended by the Imperials. He also managed to subdue trolls... and forced the invaders out of the mine! He blocked all entrances to make sure no one can reach the cave from the surface.

People say, great treasures are still there, in the caves, but all passages are blocked with rocks.

You will need to clear out these rocks and find your way to the chief goblin. His name is Gym the Cheapskate. I remember a demolition squad has been deployed there, they knew to blow up obstructions and hack through the tunnels. If you strike a bargain with them, half of the battle is won!

Oh, that is an evil place! Light forbid you end up there.

This island used to be called the Tree Island, its beauty renowned throughout the allods! Do you know of the Great Tree that gives life to all of Kania? Well, a few Kanian magi took a sprout of the Great Tree to a faraway island and grew a wondrous forest there. I visited it a number of times when I was young to drink birch sap, revel in the birds singing, and converse with sages. I was even honored to meet their mentor, Dobroslav Radov, the kindest soul there ever was...

Why "was," you might ask? Well, here's where the story gets dark. A giant spider appeared in their forest that the locals dubbed Blackvenom. No one knew where it came from, but I think the astral is to blame. Do you remember the creatures at Tenebra that were warped by the astral? This spider is like them, only stronger and much more wicked, with venom so potent it can take down a mammoth.

 So, one dark night Blackvenom scuttled up to the Tree of Life and thrust its stinger into the tree's core, poisoning all its sap. Ever since then, the tree that once bestowed life in its purest forms has been spawning vile, terrible things! The magi that walked over to the desecrated tree were themselves affected by the pollution. The spider's venom poisoned their hearts and souls...

 Dobroslav Radov, once a most gentle and wise magus, adopted the name Evildoer the Poisonous and became a cruel and ruthless maleficar! Other pagans that succumbed to the pollution massacred those who managed to keep their sanity, and are now worshiping the polluted Tree by offering bloody sacrifices. As for the forest, once beautiful and full of light, it now swarms with venomous spiders.

I beg you in the memory of my former friend Dobroslav Radov to cleanse the forest from this wickedness! Death shall be their deliverance. Kill them all, both the madmen and the spiders, but most importantly you must kill their queen, the Black Widow, and Blackvenom itself!

Are you seriously asking me this question? Rotswamp is the filthiest place in the entire astral. The soil sloshes underfoot, moisture seeps under your clothes, there are heaps of dirt swarming with insects and the fog is so thick you can't even see your own feet.

To make a long story short, you won't find a nastiest place to visit than Rotswamp! Countless travelers have gone there and never come back... And no wonder, with deadly creatures lurking at every corner! When I had the ill luck of joining an expedition to that filthy swamp, we lost three guards to hydras on the very first day. They are terrible venom-spitting creatures. We dubbed the oldest of them Echidna after it tore a pack horse in two with a single bite!

One night we awoke to horrible screaming: our camp was attacked by Lamias. Armed to their teeth, they killed our sentry and charged right at us, screaming something about two sisters craving our blood. We barely managed to fight them off!

However, in our retreat we passed through the center of the swamp, where the greatest danger of all awaited us. We had scarcely enough time to wonder why the Lamias suddenly stopped their pursuit when a gigantic drake swooped down on our group out of the night sky, spitting fire all around. Smaller drakes circled above our heads to make sure no one would escape. Miraculously, I managed to survive by falling into the mud and digging in so that the drakes couldn't see me. My companions weren't so lucky...

Come morning, when the drakes finished their bloody feast and flew away, I slinked my way back to the ship. Exhausted, wounded and covered in mud from head to toe, I nearly burst into tears when I saw the ship waiting for us. Right then and there I swore that I'd never set foot in that cursed place again!

Oh, you shouldn't be asking these questions! These questions are dangerous, you know...

I've never been to Zone 51 myself. None of the regular astral travelers has been there, either. At best they may have gotten a spyglass glimpse of a small beautiful isle bristling with thick jungle. You see, this isle is guarded by a whole army! If you get too close you're as good as astral dust.

Only Aidenus or Voisvet might know what's really on it. Rumor has it, however, that Zone 51 is the location of an Imperial military base with a research laboratory. What exactly they're researching is none of my business. All I can say is that the last visitor to that sector reported smoke rising above the isle and flashes of astral cannons. Looks like the Empire has got lab problems, again... Either the experiment's gone wrong or the lab manager is three sheets to the wind. One thing's for certain - you can't expect anything good from Zone 51! If they really did conduct experiments to create the so-called "invincible soldiers," then I'm afraid you'll have to face the consequences of their vile doings.

How do you know about this island? Did a little bird tell you? Well, well...

Alright, I'll tell you what I know. Just don't blab!

So, a while back our scouts came across an island on which June ruins have been preserved from the time the June civilization was created. As the ruins are of enormous scientific value, by the order of Aidenus himself a ship was rushed to the island bearing an archaeological expedition under the command of our best archaeologist Lisa Livingrock. The expedition reached the island and started it's dig... And that's it! All contact with them was lost. Their last message said that the scientists had almost reached the entrance to the central crypt of the June tomb. The archaeologist also complained about Kobalds, which had appeared from who knows where and were hindering their work. And then nothing, total silence. A rescue ship was sent, but I do not know whether they have returned, or if they found anything.

I guess that the scientists dug up something they shouldn't have dug up. The thirst for knowledge, just like the thirst for profit, leads to nothing good.

The Black Rock... You will recognize it immediately when you approach the island! A lifeless piece of bare rock, gouged by demonic fangs. It is teeming with demons!

As far as I know, the Black Rock is all that of left of the de Blizare House allod after the Night of Astral Portals. The de Blizare House suffered enormous losses that night. Almost all their mages fell in combat, the Great Mage took the difficult decision to abandon the allod in order to save the survivors and prepared to open a portal to Kania. Only a small squadron of volunteers was left to cover the retreat, and these were doomed to die! These heroes stood to the last and they fell as one.

But the allod survived! In spite of everything, it survived - neither the demons nor the astral were able to destroy it completely! They say that this was due to the blood of the elven martyrs, who defended their abode to the last.

If you are unlucky enough to reach the Black Rock during your travels, you should remember that there are great heroes buried here, and you should not let their memory down!

The Underwater Kingdom? Nobody can say for sure whether it exists or not. I am not able to lie, so I will tell you what I know.

I heard this story from a merchant, Gardener was his name. He was a rich merchant, he was friendly with the free traders, they say that he was planning an Oligarchy.

One day it happened that Gardner's ship wandered off the caravan trail. He saw a small island, not even an island, more like a clod of land with a well and an abandoned hut. As luck would have it, the crew's water supplies were low. They dropped anchor, and Gardener went ashore to drink some water. He had barely bent over when a cold hand reached out of the well and grabbed him by the beard! A dull voice echoed from under the water: "Promise to give me that which you have, but about which you know nothing, otherwise I will drown you!"

Gardener was scared, and he immediately promised to hand over that about which he knew nothing. If you don't know it, you won't miss it! The water spirit let him go, but as soon as the merchant reached home, he started to pull out his hair. His wife met him on the threshold with a young child. The merchant was horror struck - he had promised to give his own child to the water fiend! But it's true when they say that merchants learn to count before they can read. Gardener remembered that he was last home more than a year ago, and he could see that the child was no more than a month old! The wife was unable to balance her debit and credit columns - the child was someone else's. Gardener threw out his wayward wife along with the child, and he gave his clerk, whom he had left in charge, a good beating - the child's features were suspiciously like those of the clerk. The merchant took to the drink something chronic, and drank away his fortune, down to the last copper. And he told the water spirit, when he came at his appointed time to collect his debt, that he could sing for it, and he paid him his interest in kicks and punches.

What a sad tale. If you see a small island with a well in the astral, don't think twice, throw a barrel of explosives down the well, to teach that water fiend who reduces honest people to poverty a lesson!

Cinderland... Now that little island has no other name. But at one time it was the best hunting reserve in the Empire. My traveling companion Fedor Stablemanov said that the Great Yasker himself loved to shoot ducks or deer in this reserve. The ranger there, Kuzmich, is a famous drinker - Fedor said that there were times when they drank so much that come morning they forgot which of them was the ranger and which the traveler. Hmm, those were the days... Now only charred stumps remain, with feral beasts roaming around. It is all the fault of a mad Arisen scientist!
He was initially received as a welcome guest. And why not? A famous scientist decides to do some research in the quiet of the forest! They set up a laboratory for him in the forest, and did not inquire particularly what he was up to there. He worked away quietly until Kuzmich, that boozer, suggested that the scientist have a couple of shots with him. Well, I suppose he couldn't drink with the bears! He got into the habit of visiting the mage for a chat about science and a couple of bottles. That Orc booze would turn any normal person's brains to mush. It was nothing to Kuzmich, the Orcs have tin throats and steel livers, but the magician drank himself silly. And in a drunken fit he tore down his tower along with its foundations.
He imagined himself to be Fireborn, a Great Fire Mage, the lord of flame, damn him to hell, and he started to spray fire in all directions! That was it, an end to the reserve - he really was a Great Mage, so the forest there keeps burning but never burns out, the beasts are burned but not roasted, and worst of all, the spirit of the forest, old Oakster, fell under his spell and is now in his service. Kuzmich went off the rails with grief, he doesn't recognize anybody, just drinks and drinks. Fedor tired to reason with him, but he gave him a smack in the face and kicked him out of the hut, where there was a pack of fire wolves waiting for him. They chased Fedor right back to his ship, and burned such a hole in his trousers, it's not funny! He was lucky he didn't have his skin burned off. So, if you are planning to visit Cinderland, which is all that is left of the reserve, don't forget to bring a fire extinguisher - believe me, the flames are still blazing away there like crazy.
